description: Cassava (tapioca, karrapendalam) is a tuber crop grown from stem cuttings in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and the East Godavari area of Andhra Pradesh for food, sago and starch. It tolerates drought and poor soils, but mosaic disease spreads easily through infected planting setts.
npk_split: Apply all P with half the N and half the K at planting, and the remaining N and K at 45-60 days after planting along with earthing up.

Bacterial blight.name: Bacterial Blight
Bacterial blight.cause: Xanthomonas phaseoli pv. manihotis (syn. Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. manihotis)
Bacterial blight.description: A bacterial disease that blights the leaves and moves into the stem, causing shoot dieback in the rainy season. It is carried in infected cuttings, and antibiotics must not be used.
symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots on the leaves
Spots merge into brown blighted patches and the leaf wilts and dries
Yellowish gum drops on leaf stalks and young stems
Shoot tips die back, leaving bare stem ends
Bacterial blight.spread: Carried in infected planting setts and spread by rain splash, tools and insects during wet weather.
Bacterial blight.action: Cut out and burn affected shoots in dry weather, disinfect the knife between plants, and take planting setts only from healthy plants.

treatment.name: Healthy planting setts
treatment.notes: The main control; select setts from symptom-free plants and rotate the field with a non-host crop for one season.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP
treatment.notes: Protective only; limits spread on young plants in wet weather but does not cure infected stems.

Brown spot.name: Brown Leaf Spot
Brown spot.description: A common fungal leaf spot of older cassava leaves in warm, humid weather. It causes early fall of the lower leaves but usually little yield loss.
symptoms: Brown angular spots with a darker border on the upper leaf surface, limited by the veins
Greyish mould on the underside of the spots
Older lower leaves turn yellow and fall early
Brown spot.spread: Spores from fallen diseased leaves spread by wind and rain splash in warm, humid weather.
Brown spot.action: Collect and destroy fallen diseased leaves, and spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L only if young leaves are heavily spotted.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Seldom needed; spray only when spotting is heavy on a crop younger than 5 months.

treatment.name: Wider spacing
treatment.notes: Plant at the recommended spacing and keep the field weeded so the canopy dries quickly.

Brown streak disease.name: Brown Streak Disease
Brown streak disease.cause: Cassava brown streak virus / Ugandan cassava brown streak virus (ipomoviruses)
Brown streak disease.description: A virus disease of East and Central Africa that causes a dry brown rot inside the tubers; it is not known to occur in India. There is no curative spray, and a detection here may be a misreading of mosaic or normal leaf ageing, so get it confirmed.
symptoms: Yellow feathery patches along the smaller veins of older leaves, without leaf distortion
Brown streaks on the green part of the stem
Dry brown corky rot inside the tubers
Tubers constricted and misshapen
Brown streak disease.spread: Carried in infected planting setts and spread by whiteflies.
Brown streak disease.action: Uproot and burn the affected plants and report them to the nearest KVK or agriculture officer, because this disease is not known to occur in India.

treatment.name: Roguing and clean setts
treatment.notes: No spray cures the virus; never take planting setts from affected plants and do not move setts out of the area.

Green mite.name: Green Mite
Green mite.cause: Cassava green mite (Mononychellus tanajoa); in India similar damage is caused by spider mites (Tetranychus spp.)
Green mite.description: Tiny mites that suck sap from the young top leaves during the dry season. Leaves become speckled, small and narrow, and in heavy attack the shoot tip sheds its leaves.
symptoms: Tiny yellow pin-prick specks on young top leaves
Young leaves small, narrow and mottled
Tiny green or red mites and fine webbing on the leaf underside
Shoot tip dries and drops leaves, leaving a bare candle-stick tip
Green mite.spread: Mites are carried by wind and on planting setts and multiply fast in hot, dry weather.
Green mite.action: Spray water forcefully on the underside of the leaves every 10 days, and spray fenazaquin 10 EC 2 ml/L if the top leaves are still drying.

treatment.name: Water spray
treatment.notes: A strong jet of water on the leaf underside at 10-day intervals washes off mites in the dry season.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: For light to moderate attack; cover the underside of the top leaves.

treatment.name: Fenazaquin 10 EC
treatment.notes: Only for heavy attack; one spray, as per label, and only where the label lists your crop.

Mosaic disease.name: Mosaic Disease
Mosaic disease.cause: Indian cassava mosaic virus / Sri Lankan cassava mosaic virus (begomoviruses)
Mosaic disease.description: The most important disease of cassava in India, carried mainly in infected planting setts and also spread by whitefly. There is no curative spray, and infected plants give few, small tubers.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow and green mosaic patches on the leaves
Leaflets twisted, distorted and smaller than normal
Stunted plants
Few, small tubers
Mosaic disease.spread: Spreads mainly through setts taken from infected plants and from plant to plant by whiteflies.
Mosaic disease.action: Uproot and burn mosaic plants as soon as they are seen and take setts for the next crop only from symptom-free plants.

treatment.name: Mosaic-free setts and roguing
treatment.notes: No spray cures the virus; mark healthy plants during the season and use only their stems for planting.

treatment.name: Resistant varieties
treatment.notes: Grow mosaic-resistant varieties such as Sree Padmanabha or Sree Reksha where the disease is severe.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: Whitefly control only, in the first 3 months; install yellow sticky traps.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or nutrient problem. Mark such plants as a source of healthy planting setts.
symptoms: Uniform green, fully opened hand-shaped leaves
No mosaic, spots, specks or distortion
Normal leaf size and steady new growth
healthy.action: Continue fortnightly scouting and mark healthy plants for taking planting setts.
